+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1MNYFW81216M57PS9NDZKBE
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8680'
+title: 'run subcommand: one turn in process over InMemoryTransport.pair()'
+---
+## What
+
+cli-plan.md §4 and §5.4. This is the product CLI: one prompt in, one
+turn, exit.
+
+**The one architecture rule: the CLI reaches the agent through an ACP
+connection.** It must never call `RoutedACPAgent` directly. Only the
+transport changes between the modes. Break this rule and the later
+socket mode becomes a rewrite, and the CLI stops proving the protocol.
+
+In `Sources/acp-agent/RunCommand.swift`:
+
+1. Build the agent with the shared `AgentComposition` of the `acp` task.
+2. `InMemoryTransport.pair()` gives two transports. Bind an
+   `AgentSideConnection` on one, and a `ClientSideConnection` on the
+   other, in one process and with no subprocess. This is the method the
+   Mac app uses (`plan.md` §19).
+3. Drive the turn from the client side: `initialize`, `session/new` with
+   the `cwd`, `session/prompt`, then consume the notifications until a
+   stop reason arrives.
+
+Options in this task: `--cwd <path>` and `--resume <session-id>`.
+`--cwd` selects **which** dotfolder stack the loader reads, so apply it
+before the configuration load, and send the same directory in
+`session/new` (§5.10). `--cwd` together with `--resume` is a usage
+error: the stored session already has a working directory, and it wins.
+
+`--verbose`, `--quiet`, the stdout rules and the exit codes are separate
+tasks. Print the answer plainly here.
+
+- [ ] Pair the two connections in process
+- [ ] Drive initialize, session/new and session/prompt
+- [ ] `--cwd` before the configuration load, and in `session/new`
+- [ ] `--resume` through `session/load`
+- [ ] `--cwd` with `--resume` is a usage error
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `swift run acp-agent run "hello"` runs one turn and prints the
+      answer.
+- [ ] No file in `Sources/acp-agent/` names `RoutedACPAgent` outside
+      `AgentComposition.swift`. The CLI talks to a connection.
+- [ ] `--cwd` with `--resume` exits 2 with a message on stderr.
+- [ ] `--cwd` changes which `config.yaml` the process loads.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/RunCommandTests.swift`: with
+      the scripted model of the shared test support, a `run` turn over
+      the in-process pair gives the scripted answer.
+- [ ] `--cwd` with `--resume` is a usage error, exit 2.
+- [ ] An integration test builds two temporary directories with
+      different `config.yaml` files, and asserts that `--cwd` selects
+      the matching resolved configuration.
+- [ ] A source-level test asserts that no file in `Sources/acp-agent/`
+      other than `AgentComposition.swift` holds the string
+      `RoutedACPAgent`. It pins the architecture rule.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,6 +1,55 @@
 ---
 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m1x2gqade3essyw5bz15h3nq
+  text: |-
+    Research and design notes for the next agent.
+
+    **The architecture pin needed one move before it could pass.**
+    `Sources/acp-agent/AcpAgentCommand.swift` held `RoutedACPAgent.buildVersion`
+    in its `CommandConfiguration`. So the source-level test the card asks for
+    failed on a file that has nothing to do with the turn. The version now
+    stands as `AgentComposition.version`, and `AcpAgentCommand.swift` no longer
+    imports the library. `AgentComposition.swift` is the one file that names
+    the agent type.
+
+    **One bind, not two.** `AcpCommand` and the new `RunTurn` both need an
+    `AgentSideConnection` around the composed agent. That bind is now
+    `AgentComposition.Composed.serve(over:logger:)`, so the two modes cannot
+    drift and no other file names the agent type. `acp` passes
+    `logger: .standardError`; `run` takes the `.disabled` default, because
+    §5.7 says a default run writes nothing to stderr.
+
+    **`--resume` needs the recorded cwd, and the CLI does not know it.**
+    `ResumeSessionRequest` carries a required `cwd`, and the agent refuses a
+    resume whose `cwd` does not equal the recorded one (plan.md §7.4). The run
+    therefore reads the directory off the unfiltered, paged `session/list`
+    before it calls `session/load`. That is the whole reason `--cwd` beside
+    `--resume` is a usage error. An id no page carries gives
+    `UnknownResumedSessionError`; the run never degrades into a fresh session.
+
+    **`Composed` now carries the start-up configuration.** It is the value the
+    `--cwd` proof reads, and it is the first of the two loads of §5.10.
+
+    **The scripted model records no transcript entries for a text delta.**
+    `ScriptedSessionBackend` appends SDK entries for tool calls only, so a
+    resume over it has nothing to restore. The resume proof uses
+    `ResumeRecordingContainer` of `ResumeSessionFixture.swift` instead, which
+    appends real prompt, reasoning and response entries.
+
+    **Two shared test helpers grew, and no fixture was copied.**
+    `ConfigCommandFixture` gained `stubEnvironment` (the config home plus
+    `ACP_AGENT_STUB_MODEL=1`) and `writeProjectCompactionTrigger(_:)` (the
+    inert key that names which project layer a load read).
+
+    **Out of scope, and left alone on purpose.** `--out-of-process`,
+    `--verbose` and `--quiet` parse and do nothing, which is the state they
+    were already in and the state their own cards change. The §5.5 stdin rows
+    belong to the prompt-source card: an absent prompt argument is a usage
+    error here.
+  timestamp: 2026-09-07T04:37:40.813581+00:00
